title: Looking up APB fields by meaning
text:
Introduction
The AnnData Proteomics Bridge (APB) converts the reports of quantification software such as DIA-NN, Spectronaut or MaxQuant into one result layout. The columns keep the vendors’ names, so a posterior error probability is PEP in MaxQuant and EG_PEP in Spectronaut. apb-catalog records what each column means; apbCatalogR implements its API in R, so an R application asks for a meaning and gets the column or its data.
The package works on a bundle apb-catalog releases: the APB parse rules and the reviewed catalogue sets. One bundle ships with the package, together with a test bundle of synthetic results and the answers apb-catalog gives on them.
Installation

install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("anndata-omics-bridge/apbCatalogR")


library(apbCatalogR)
catalog_version()
#> $version
#> [1] "0.1.1"
#> 
#> $origin
#> [1] "shipped"
#> 
#> $path
#> [1] "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/apbCatalogR/extdata/bundle"
#> 
#> $apb2_version
#> [1] "0.1.1"

Catalogue sets
Each catalogue set serves one kind of consumer:

catalogues()[, c("catalogue", "has_requirements", "entries")]
#>                catalogue has_requirements entries
#> 1              abundance             TRUE      48
#> 2             confidence            FALSE      22
#> 3 proteobench_entrapment            FALSE       7
#> 4                    apb             TRUE      66
#> 5         chromatography            FALSE      54

Which column a software version reports
Catalog answers from the rules alone, without data:

diann <- Catalog$new("DIA-NN", "2.2.0", "abundance")
diann$layer("peptidoform_ion", kind = "intensity", normalization = "none")
#> <Reference peptidoform_ion layers: Precursor_Quantity>
diann$kinds("peptidoform_ion", "layers")
#> [1] "intensity"     "ms1_intensity"

The data of a result
read_parsed_levels() reads a Parquet result apb2 wrote, one anndataR AnnData per level. The test bundle carries synthetic results; this one has MaxQuant’s peptidoform-ion level.

results <- tempfile()
utils::untar(system.file("extdata", "test-bundle", "results.tar.gz", package = "apbCatalogR"), exdir = results)
result <- read_parsed_levels(file.path(results, "maxquant_wide-peptidoform_ion.parquet"))
result
#> <ParsedLevels>
#>   peptidoform_ion: 2 x 3, layers: Intensity, MS_MS_Count, Retention_Time, Retention_Length, Calibrated_Retention_Time, Calibrated_Retention_Time_Start, Calibrated_Retention_Time_Finish, Score, PEP

DataCatalog answers on the result and hands back the data:

confidence <- DataCatalog$new(result, "confidence")
pep <- confidence$layer("peptidoform_ion", kind = "pep")
dim(pep)
#> [1] 2 3

MaxQuant reports no q-value on this level, so that lookup gives NULL:

confidence$layer("peptidoform_ion", kind = "q_value")
#> NULL

A lookup that several fields answer signals UnresolvedField rather than choosing silently. DIA-NN 1.8 reports both an unnormalized and a normalized intensity per precursor:

tryCatch(
  Catalog$new("DIA-NN", "1.8.1", "abundance")$layer("peptidoform_ion", kind = "intensity"),
  UnresolvedField = function(condition) conditionMessage(condition)
)
#> [1] "kind=intensity on peptidoform_ion is ambiguous: 2 entries match: Precursor_Quantity, Precursor_Normalised; candidates: Precursor_Quantity, Precursor_Normalised"

Rule coverage
rule_coverage() checks every rule against one set; a set with requirements judges each level:

coverage <- rule_coverage("abundance")
unique(coverage[, c("software", "version", "level", "verdict")])[1:5, ]
#>    software version           level verdict
#> 1  AlphaDIA    1.10 peptidoform_ion    warn
#> 3  AlphaDIA    1.12 peptidoform_ion    warn
#> 5  AlphaDIA     2.x peptidoform_ion    warn
#> 7  AlphaDIA     2.x         protein    <NA>
#> 8 AlphaPept     0.5 peptidoform_ion    pass

A newer catalog
update_catalog() downloads the bundle of the latest apb-catalog release into the user cache; later sessions use the newest bundle, shipped or downloaded. It works from the next apb-catalog release, the first to ship the bundle.

update_catalog()

title: apbCatalogR 0.99.0
text:
apbCatalogR 0.99.0

First version: apb-catalog’s API in R on the apb-catalog bundle: the R6 classes Catalog, DataCatalog and Reference, catalogues(), rule_coverage(), catalogue_table() and the conditions UnresolvedField, StaleField and MissingRequiredField.
read_parsed_levels() reads an APB Parquet result into ParsedLevels, one anndataR AnnData per level. It also reads apb2’s .h5ad and .duckdb results into the same ParsedLevels; Parquet needs the suggested arrow package and DuckDB the suggested duckdb and DBI packages; .h5ad needs only anndataR 1.2.2 or later, the first to read the text columns apb2 writes.
update_catalog() downloads the bundle of an apb-catalog release; catalog_version() reports the bundle in use.
The bundle holds only the rules and catalogue sets; the synthetic results and expected answers ship as a separate test bundle in inst/extdata/test-bundle/.
Snapshots are not ported: DataCatalog$snapshot(), $resolve(), attach_snapshot(), stored_snapshot(), stale_levels() and ResolutionSnapshot have no R counterpart.

title: apbCatalogR
text:
Every catalogue set of the bundle with its purpose, its users and its number of entries.

catalogues()


A data frame with columns catalogue, purpose, used_by (a list column), has_requirements and entries.


library("apbCatalogR")

catalogues()

               catalogue
1              abundance
2             confidence
3 proteobench_entrapment
4                    apb
5         chromatography
                                                                                                                                                    purpose
1                                                What each layer an APB2 rule marks abundance measures, and whether the software normalizes it across runs.
2                                    How likely each identification, or the signal quantified for it, is correct: PEP and q-values per run and per feature.
3                                                                      The precursor q-values ProteoBench's entrapment scoring ranks by, each its own kind.
4 The fields APB writes itself for every vendor, asked for by kind: ProForma identifiers, decoy and contaminant flags, role columns and sample annotations.
5                                                         Retention times, elution-peak bounds and peak widths, with the unit the software reports them in.
       used_by has_requirements entries
1 apb-prot....             TRUE      48
2 apb-aggr....            FALSE      22
3 apb-prot....            FALSE       7
4 apb-expo....             TRUE      66
5 apb-expo....            FALSE      54

title: apbCatalogR
text:
Reads a result apb2 wrote into a ParsedLevels object, one anndataR AnnData per level, the same for every format: a .h5ad file, a .duckdb file, or the directory apb2 writes for a .parquet result. Reading Parquet needs the arrow package, DuckDB the duckdb and DBI packages; .h5ad needs nothing beyond anndataR.

read_parsed_levels(path)




path


The result, such as converted.h5ad, converted.duckdb or the directory converted.parquet.


A ParsedLevels object.


library("apbCatalogR")

results <- tempfile()
archive <- system.file("extdata", "test-bundle", "results.tar.gz", package = "apbCatalogR")
utils::untar(archive, exdir = results)
read_parsed_levels(file.path(results, "edge-two-levels.parquet"))

Which column one software version reports for each meaning

Answers from the rules alone, without data. The rule of the software whose version pattern admits the version decides which fields each level has. Lookups that several fields answer, or that an unreviewed level cannot, signal UnresolvedField.

The class generator; Catalog$new() returns a Catalog.




description

Catalog$new()


Catalog$kinds()

Catalog$var()

Catalog$fields()


Catalog$print()


Catalog$clone()





Bind a catalogue set to the rule levels of one software version.


Catalog\$new(software, version, catalog, enforce = NULL)





software


The software name, such as “DIA-NN”.


version


The software version, such as “2.2.0”.


catalog


The catalogue set, such as “abundance” or “confidence”; see catalogues().


enforce


NULL, “MUST” or “SHOULD”: signal MissingRequiredField when a field the set requires at that strength is missing.






The kinds the level offers at one location, given the other qualifiers.


Catalog\$kinds(level, location, ...)





level


The quantification level.


location


“layers”, “var” or “obs”.


…


Other qualifiers by name, such as normalization = “none”.




A character vector.



Where the sample-by-feature layer with this meaning lives.


Catalog\$layer(level, kind, ...)





level


The quantification level.


kind


The kind, such as “intensity”.


…


Other qualifiers by name.




A Reference, or NULL when the level has no such layer.



Where the per-feature column with this meaning lives, in var or a varm table.


Catalog\$var(level, kind, ...)





level


The quantification level.


kind


The kind.


…


Other qualifiers by name.




A Reference, or NULL.



Where the per-sample column with this meaning lives.


Catalog\$obs(level, kind, ...)





level


The quantification level.


kind


The kind.


…


Other qualifiers by name.




A Reference, or NULL.



Every catalogued field the rule declares, one row per field, as catalogue_table() shows them.


Catalog\$fields()


A data frame, with present true for each row.



Print the set and the levels.


Catalog\$print(...)





…


Ignored.






The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.


Catalog\$clone(deep = FALSE)





deep


Whether to make a deep clone.

title: apbCatalogR
text:
Downloads the bundle of an apb-catalog release from GitHub into the user cache, so lookups use it without a package update. Later sessions keep using the newest bundle, shipped or downloaded. It works from the next apb-catalog release, the first to ship the bundle.

update_catalog(version = NULL)




version


The apb-catalog release, such as “0.2.0”; NULL downloads the latest release.


The catalog_version() now in use, invisibly.


library("apbCatalogR")

if (interactive()) {
  update_catalog()
}

title: apbCatalogR
text:
Downloads the bundle of an apb-catalog release from GitHub into the user cache, so lookups use it without a package update. Later sessions keep using the newest bundle, shipped or downloaded. It works from the next apb-catalog release, the first to ship the bundle.

update_catalog(version = NULL)




version


The apb-catalog release, such as “0.2.0”; NULL downloads the latest release.


The catalog_version() now in use, invisibly.


library("apbCatalogR")

if (interactive()) {
  update_catalog()
}

title: apbCatalogR
text:
One row per entry and rule it applies to, as apb-catalog table prints it.

catalogue_table(catalogue = NULL)




catalogue


One set’s name; NULL lists every set of the bundle.


A data frame with columns set, source (the vendor, producer:<name> or annotation:<convention>), version_pattern, rule (* for an entry of every rule), level, location, table, name (role:<role> or prefix:<prefix> for a field found by role or column-name prefix), one qualifier.<name> column per qualifier, requirement and entry_id.

title: apbCatalogR
text:
One APB result: its levels on one observation axis
One APB result: its levels on one observation axis

The R counterpart of apb2’s ParsedLevels, as read_parsed_levels() returns it.
Each level is an anndataR AnnData laid out as apb2’s .h5ad writer lays it out: the primary layer in X, the other layers in layers, obs and var frames named by their key columns, and the level’s APB part in uns$apb: parse (with provenance$rule_json), roles, storage and post-parse records.

The class generator; ParsedLevels$new() returns a ParsedLevels object.




levels


A named list of anndataR AnnData, one per level.


uns


The root parse record.


metadata


The root post-parse records, such as sdrf or fasta.


hierarchy


How the levels nest, or NULL.


annotation_tables


A named list of data frames; each carries its metadata as the attribute apb.


feature_relations


A named list of data frames of source, row, target, column and value; each carries its metadata as the attribute apb.







ParsedLevels$new()


ParsedLevels$print()


ParsedLevels$clone()





Collect the levels and records of one result.


ParsedLevels\$new(
  levels,
  uns = list(),
  metadata = list(),
  hierarchy = NULL,
  annotation_tables = list(),
  feature_relations = list()
)





levels


A named list of anndataR AnnData.


uns


The root parse record.


metadata


The root post-parse records.


hierarchy


How the levels nest, or NULL.


annotation_tables


A named list of data frames.


feature_relations


A named list of data frames.






Print the levels and their shapes.


ParsedLevels\$print(...)

ParsedLevels\$clone(deep = FALSE)

Whether to make a deep clone.

results <- tempfile()
archive <- system.file("extdata", "test-bundle", "results.tar.gz", package = "apbCatalogR")

result <- read_parsed_levels(file.path(results, "edge-two-levels.parquet"))

title: apbCatalogR
text:
One row per catalogued or required field of each rule level the set reviews; a set without vendor catalogues is checked against every rule level. A set with requirements judges each level: fail when a MUST field is unsupported, warn when a SHOULD or MAY field is, pass otherwise.

rule_coverage(catalogue)




catalogue


The set’s name.


A data frame with columns software, version, rule, level, kind, qualifiers (the other qualifiers as key=value), origin, producer (NA for the vendor’s own fields), requirement, location, table, column (NA when unsupported), inputs (a list column of the vendor columns apb2 computes the column from), needs (what to run before the field exists) and verdict (NA for a set without requirements).


library("apbCatalogR")

head(rule_coverage("abundance"))

  software version                      rule           level      kind
1 AlphaDIA    1.10 alphadia/v1_10/rules.json peptidoform_ion intensity
2 AlphaDIA    1.10 alphadia/v1_10/rules.json peptidoform_ion directlfq
3 AlphaDIA    1.12 alphadia/v1_12/rules.json peptidoform_ion intensity
4 AlphaDIA    1.12 alphadia/v1_12/rules.json peptidoform_ion directlfq
5 AlphaDIA     2.x    alphadia/v2/rules.json peptidoform_ion intensity
6 AlphaDIA     2.x    alphadia/v2/rules.json peptidoform_ion directlfq
                 qualifiers origin producer requirement location table
1        normalization=none   <NA>       NA      SHOULD   layers  <NA>
2 normalization=run_setting   <NA>       NA        <NA>   layers  <NA>
3        normalization=none   <NA>       NA      SHOULD   layers  <NA>
4 normalization=run_setting   <NA>       NA        <NA>   layers  <NA>
5        normalization=none   <NA>       NA      SHOULD   layers  <NA>
6 normalization=run_setting   <NA>       NA        <NA>   layers  <NA>
               column inputs needs verdict
1                <NA>         <NA>    warn
2           Intensity         <NA>    warn
3                <NA>         <NA>    warn
4           Intensity         <NA>    warn
5                <NA>         <NA>    warn
6 Precursor_Intensity         <NA>    warn

title: apbCatalogR
text:
apb-catalog’s API in R: look up the fields of an APB result by meaning, such as a PEP or an unnormalized intensity, without naming vendor columns.

New API. This package is new, and its API may still change between releases. Feedback is very welcome: open an issue with what you need, what surprised you, or what broke.

Documentation: anndata-omics-bridge.github.io/apbCatalogR, with the vignette as the walkthrough.


The AnnData Proteomics Bridge, apb2, converts the reports of proteomics quantification software into one result layout. Declarative parse rules describe each vendor table, so one parser reads them all.

Software: AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, FragPipe, MaxQuant, PEAKS, Sage, Spectronaut and more
Levels: peptidoform ion, peptidoform, peptide, protein, peptidoform fragment
Per level: one AnnData, runs as obs, features as var, measurements as layers
Formats: h5ad, h5mu, Parquet, DuckDB

Columns keep the vendor’s names: the posterior error probability is PEP in MaxQuant and DIA-NN, EG_PEP in Spectronaut.



apb-catalog records what those columns mean, in reviewed catalogue sets. A consumer asks a set for a kind, such as pep or intensity, and gets the column.







Set
Fields




abundance
Intensities, and whether the software normalizes them across runs


confidence
PEP and q-values per run and per feature


proteobench_entrapment
Precursor q-values for ProteoBench’s entrapment scoring


apb
Fields APB writes for every vendor: ProForma identifiers, decoy and contaminant flags, sample annotations


chromatography
Retention times, peak bounds and widths, with their unit



A lookup answers one of three ways:

One field: the column, or its data
Software does not report it: NULL
Several fields: an UnresolvedField error, never a silent choice




apbCatalogR is apb-catalog’s Python API in R, as R6 classes with the same names and methods. Snapshots are not ported: DataCatalog$snapshot(), $resolve(), attach_snapshot(), stored_snapshot(), stale_levels() and ResolutionSnapshot have no R counterpart. It needs no Python: the rules and catalogues come from a bundle shipped with the package.







Call
Answers




Catalog$new(software, version, set)
From the rules alone, without data


DataCatalog$new(result, set)
On one result, and returns the data


catalogues(), rule_coverage(), catalogue_table()
The sets, how each rule covers a set, every entry as a table


read_parsed_levels(path)
An APB result, .h5ad, .parquet or .duckdb, as ParsedLevels, one anndataR AnnData per level



It does not convert vendor files. Convert with apb2; any of its h5ad, Parquet or DuckDB results reads the same:
apb2 convert DATA --params PARAMETER_FILE --format parquet --output result   # writes result.parquet



install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("anndata-omics-bridge/apbCatalogR")
Reading .h5ad results needs nothing more. Parquet results need arrow, DuckDB results duckdb and DBI:
install.packages(c("arrow", "duckdb", "DBI"))



Ask the rules which column a software version reports:
library(apbCatalogR)
diann <- Catalog$new("DIA-NN", "2.2.0", "abundance")
diann$kinds("peptidoform_ion", "layers")
#> [1] "intensity"     "ms1_intensity"
diann$layer("peptidoform_ion", kind = "intensity", normalization = "none")
#> <Reference peptidoform_ion layers: Precursor_Quantity>
Get the data of a result:
result <- read_parsed_levels("result.parquet")
confidence <- DataCatalog$new(result, "confidence")
pep <- confidence$layer("peptidoform_ion", kind = "pep")   # runs x features matrix



apb-catalog builds two bundles at each release:

Bundle: apb2’s parse rules and the reviewed catalogue sets; lookups read only this
Test bundle: synthetic results, with apb-catalog’s answers on them; the tests check that R gives the same answers

How R gets the latest bundle:

Shipped: inst/extdata/bundle/, with the test bundle in inst/extdata/test-bundle/, both replaced by a pull request from each apb-catalog release
update_catalog(): downloads the latest release’s bundle into the user cache; works from the next apb-catalog release, the first to ship the bundle
Each session uses the newest bundle, shipped or downloaded; catalog_version() reports which
